topic: master cron fires ~7min after nominal tick — breaks ±2min match window
root_cause_hypothesis: CronCreate docs say jobs fire only while REPL is idle, and recurring jitter is up to 10% of period (1.5min for */15). Observed 7min drift exceeds jitter spec — likely caused by Claude being mid-query at nominal tick, deferring fire until idle.
impact: All */15 slots in cowork-schedule.json fire at :00,:15,:30,:45. Matcher window at the deferred fire time (e.g. :07) is [05-09] which never contains :00. Every fire produces silent-exit even when slots should match. The dispatcher will never actually spawn agents at the drift rate observed.
options_for_architect: A. Widen matcher window to ±10min (covers 7min drift but creates overlap between adjacent ticks — needs collision rule reconsidered)
B. Use nominal-tick rounding: round current minute down to nearest 15 to compute the intended tick, then match against that minute ±2. This handles drift cleanly.
C. Drop master-cron pattern — fall back to per-slot CronCreate (loses sub-hourly RemoteTrigger advantage but each slot fires independently with own jitter)
recommendation: Option B — minimum-diff fix in .claude/scripts/cowork-match-slots.js. Architect should decide.
router_action: kept master cron ed39cbcf active for now; legacy RemoteTriggers still cover slots during 24h parallel-run — no production gap. But cutover at 2026-05-19T20:34Z must be blocked until drift is resolved.
